chunks: Through his chain, he said: We discussed the Qa'im (the Rising One) in his presence, so he said: His name is the name of the barber's scalpel.

key_terms.الْقَائِمَ: The Rising One, a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the name of Imam al-Qa'im being compared to a barber's scalpel?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Qa'im (the Mahdi) is identified by the name 'Musa', linked etymologically to 'al-Haddad' (the barber/scalpel), a title often associated with the barber of the Imams. This highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of connecting the Mahdi's identity to the lineage of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), reinforcing the continuity of the Imamate during the period of occultation.
